Cc: procurement@quantumhealth.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment commercial ask — platform fee, support SLAs, and onboarding credits

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the consistent latency and the migration story for our on-prem clusters. Procurement asked me to follow up with concrete questions so we can finalize the commercial term sheet. Would you confirm the following so we can build the SOW: 

1) Platform fee treatment: is the platform fee a percentage of committed spend or a fixed annual flat fee? We are evaluating both approaches and need an example cost schedule.
2) Support tiers and SLAs: we need an explicit breakdown for Standard / Premium / Enterprise (response / P1/P2 times, annual credits, number of on-call engineers included).
3) Onboarding & migration credits: do you offer a time-limited credit for a multi-year commit? If so, what is the typical duration and uplift?
4) Exit / data return costs: what are any fees associated with offboarding from a VPC/on-prem contract?

Attached is an initial SOW draft (QH_SOW_DRAFT_v2.pdf) and a spreadsheet where we are modeling annual run-rate (platform_fee_workbook.xlsx). Looking to get ballpark answers by next Wednesday so we can present to Finance on 5/29.

Best,
Carmen Soto
Head of Procurement, Quantum Health

Subject: Re: Private deployment commercial ask — platform fee, support SLAs, and onboarding credits

Carmen —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers and I'll flag a couple of variants below so you can see tradeoffs. I'm copying Marissa (sales lead for strategic accounts) and Priyom (commercial ops) in case you want a modeled workbook.

1) Platform fee: we support both models. Typical choices we see:
   - Fixed annual platform fee (recommended for budget predictability): flat fee that covers control-plane costs, continuous updates, and licensing for Redwood Console. Example: $150k/year for deployments of up to 8 dedicated GPUs; scales discretely by SKU thereafter.
   - Percentage of committed spend: 10% of committed infra spend annually (useful for variable infra footprints).

   For your model sheet, we can show both. If you sign a 3-year committed capacity, we can discount the platform fee (see below).

2) Support tiers (summary):
   - Standard: 9x5 email + ticket triage, P1 response <8 business hours, 2 on-call engineering hours/month, quarterly health checks.
   - Premium: 24x7 on-call, P1 response <2 hours, 8 on-call engineering hours/month, monthly health reviews, 8 incident credits/year.
   - Enterprise (Platinum): 24x7 named on-call, P1 response <1 hour, 24 on-call engineering hours/month, weekly ops reviews, unlimited incident handling within SLA (subject to fair use).

3) Onboarding credits: standard is 1 month of platform fee credited (or up to $25k) for a 1-year commit. For 3-year commits we typically provide 3 months or a $75k onboarding credit. We also include up to 40 engineer-hours for migration during onboarding for the 3-year program.

4) Exit & data return: we don't charge for returning customer data. If there's an extended offboarding support engagement (hands-on migration by Redwood engineers past the included onboarding hours) that is billed at standard engineering rates or can be included as a fixed offboarding SOW.

I attach a short workbook with two example price ladders; Marissa / Priyom — can you take a pass on a 3-year commitment example for Quantum Health and the incremental discount frameworks? Carmen — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that would help.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Aditya / Priyom — forwarding Carmen's ask and your responses. Drafting a priced option set for a recommended 3-year program. Key trade-offs I'm assuming:

- Offer A (Balanced): 3-year commit, flat platform fee with 12% discount, 3 months onboarding credit, 40 eng-hours included, Premium support.
- Offer B (Aggressive): 3-year commit, 18% discount, 6 months onboarding credit, 80 eng-hours, Enterprise support — requires approval for revenue exposure by Finance (higher credit).
- Offer C (Conservative): 1-year commit, 5% discount, 1 month onboarding credit, Standard support.

Thoughts: for Quantum Health (sensitive data, expected expansion), Offer A gives predictability and keeps platform-fee revenue visible. Offer B is attractive but we should tie the extra credits to milestones (staged deployment, 2x capacity milestone).

Priyom — can you produce a revenue exposure calc for Offer B and a suggested approval note for Finance? I can draft the commercial term memo for Carmen.

Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Aditya — attached is the quick exposure model (platform_fee_workbook.xlsx) with net present value and an early-termination sensitivity. Highlights:

- Offer A (12% disc): NPV over 3 years = $1.08M; offboarding risk low.
- Offer B (18% disc + 6mo credit): NPV = $0.92M; requires a $120k finance waiver for onboarding credit timing (we defer revenue recognition in year 1).
- Offer C (1-year): NPV = $0.37M with higher churn risk.

Recommendation: propose Offer A as baseline; include Offer B as a negotiated counter if Quantum needs stronger onboarding support — but make the 6-month credit conditional on hitting a capacity milestone (50% of committed GPUs in production within 9 months).

I've added language for an offboarding clause: "No data egress fees for standard data export (up to 5TB). Extended migration assistance billed at $X/hr or covered by consumed onboarding hours." Also included a limited ROI rebate if Quantum migrates to a different provider within first 12 months (safety for customer).

Attached: platform_fee_workbook.xlsx (revenue scenarios).

Priyom
Commercial Ops

Aditya — thank you and team for the quick turnaround. Quantum's internal stakeholders reviewed Offer A and B. We are inclined to accept Offer A as the primary term, but want the following clarifications before we sign: 

1) Can the platform fee be invoiced quarterly in advance rather than annual invoicing? (helps our cashflow).
2) For the 12% discount in Offer A, will Redwood agree to a 30-day SLA for response on P2 incidents (currently listed as P2 response <8 hours)? We want that tightened for the first 6 months of production.
3) We need the offboarding clause in writing (no data egress fees up to 5TB and a defined hourly rate for extended migration assistance).

If you can provide a redline-ready term sheet with those three changes, we should be able to get sign-off from Procurement + Legal next week. I will also attach a short procurement checklist in a follow-up email.

Thanks,
Carmen Soto
Head of Procurement, Quantum Health
